propositions: A colon in a model id (e.g. anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0) is incorrectly treated as a provider qualifier by a shape regex, discarding configured provider values
A typo in an explicitly configured provider (e.g. 'bedrok' instead of 'bedrock') is not caught at config-resolution time but only at provider construction, making debugging harder

The shape-based regex test is fragile: any future model id matching the identifier pattern becomes incorrectly promoted to a provider qualifier, and slashed names like 'gateway/openai' are wrongly rejected
Provider qualification should be decided by membership in a known-provider registry, not by string shape heuristics, following LangChain and LiteLLM precedent
An explicitly configured provider must be validated against a static frozenset of known names and raise LLMConfigError early if it is not recognized
An inline unrecognized prefix in a model string should remain unqualified and pass through unchanged, permitting colon-bearing model ids to survive intact
